ก่อนมีอาคารถาวร โรงเรียนเต้าหมิงเปิดสอนภ: Before having a permanent building, Tao Ming School unofficially taught Chinese by private individuals. When the Private Schools Act of 1918 (B.E. 2461) came into effect, the school formally requested establishment in 1920 (B.E. 2463) using the name “To Beng” according to the Hokkien Chinese accent, before changing its name to “Tao Ming” according to the Mandarin Chinese accent. This term means guiding towards knowledge.
อาคารที่ยังเห็นอยู่สร้างขึ้นใน พ.ศ. 2465: The still-visible building was built in 1922 (B.E. 2465) with funds raised from mining tycoons and Chinese merchants in the old market, Yan Yao area, including merchant networks from Ranong and Phuket. Another official source described it as the work of the Chinese Merchants Association who came to mine tin, so that Chinese descendants could learn the Chinese language. Therefore, the applied Sino-Portuguese building with a zinc roof is not just a school, but evidence that the wealth from mining, trade, and Chinese networks was transforming into a community institution.
ในเวลานั้นตะกั่วป่าเป็นย่านการค้าและขนส่: At that time, Takua Pa was a trading and transportation hub tied to the river and the sea. The town grew from tin ore, with Chinese from Hokkien, Guangdong, and Hainan coming in as laborers, merchants, and entrepreneurs. The school served to reinforce language and cultural roots for the Chinese community in the prospering mining town.
แหล่งข้อมูลท้องถิ่นระบุว่าเหมืองแร่ตะกั่: Local sources indicate that Takua Pa tin mines gradually closed down since the 1970s (B.E. 2520s), reducing the town's liveliness, while Tao Ming School went out of business later. Verifiable official sources only confirm that “the school has been cancelled” and the building is under the care of the Tao Ming School Takua Pa Foundation, but do not specify the year of closure or details of the handover.
ยังไม่พบหลักฐานอ่านได้ที่ยืนยันว่าอาคารไ: No readable evidence has been found to verify that the building was directly affected by the 2004 (B.E. 2547) tsunami or was restored in any specific year. Therefore, it should not be concluded that it was damaged or repaired from that event, even though the Takua Pa area has places related to tsunami victim management and the old town has revived its role in cultural tourism.
เอกสารขอบเขตเมืองเก่าของ ONEP ระบุแนวเขต: The old town boundary document by ONEP indicates the boundary passing through Tao Ming School, and the community database of the Sirindhorn Anthropology Centre classifies the building among the important evidence of the old town. However, this search has not yet found a Fine Arts Department announcement directly registering the “Tao Ming School Building”. Therefore, the conservation status of the area is separated from the registration status of the building.
